headline: iOS 27 lets you save video frames as photos in Apple Photos
summary: A highly requested feature is finally arriving in Apple's Photos app with iOS 27, allowing users to extract still images directly from their videos.
details: Apple is rolling out a significant update to its Photos app with the upcoming iOS 27 release. Among the new features is the ability to save individual frames from videos as standalone photos within your library.
This long-awaited functionality addresses a common user request, making it easier than ever to capture the perfect still moment from a video without needing third-party tools or complex editing.

The update is expected to be part of the broader iOS 27 software package, which typically launches in the fall. Users will be able to select a video, pause it at the desired frame, and then save that frame as a new photo.
This feature streamlines the process of creating a photo library that is rich with both captured stills and high-quality stills extracted from video content.

headline_marked: AI Memory Shortage [[Drives Up Car Prices]] — GM Warns of $2B Cost Increase
headline: AI Memory Shortage Drives Up Car Prices — GM Warns of $2B Cost Increase
summary: The AI-driven memory chip shortage is now impacting the automotive sector, with GM expecting a $1.5-$2 billion cost increase and BYD hiking driver assistance feature prices by 20%.
details: The global shortage of AI memory chips is extending its reach beyond consumer electronics and into the automotive industry. General Motors projects its costs to rise by $1.5 to $2 billion this year, primarily due to escalating prices for vehicle components, especially DRAM.

This surge in costs is attributed to the increasing complexity of modern vehicles. While older models required minimal memory, today's cars are packed with advanced features and technologies, demanding significantly more memory for systems like infotainment, ADAS, and centralized computing.

Micron estimates that the average vehicle will require 278GB of DRAM and NAND by 2026, a substantial jump from the 90GB used in 2023. High-end models could demand up to 2TB, with AI assistants alone requiring at least 256GB.

Automotive-grade memory chips are specialized and require extensive validation, taking months or years to approve due to stringent environmental and performance standards. This specialized nature exacerbates the impact of the current shortage.

BYD, a major Chinese automaker, has already responded by increasing prices for its driver assistance features by 20%. Hyundai has also urged domestic chip manufacturers to bolster the local supply chain.

The ongoing memory chip shortage is poised to significantly affect the automotive industry, leading to higher vehicle prices for consumers already facing record-high costs. If the situation persists, it could also result in delivery delays and reduced vehicle availability.
